title: Collaborative Knowledge Stewardship
definition: The practice of managing and curating shared knowledge in a collaborative context, with emphasis on maintaining an up-to-date, accurate, and organized knowledge base.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine you and a group of friends are building a garden. To grow the best plants, you need to regularly check and update your seeds, tools, and notes. This is like collaborative knowledge stewardship — ensuring your shared knowledge is current and helpful.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Collaborative knowledge stewardship involves maintaining a knowledge base that is accurate, up-to-date, and organized. This ensures that everyone has access to the most relevant and useful information. In the context of CADMIES, this means managing scientific notes, training data, and models.
difficulty_levels.expert: Collaborative knowledge stewardship is a complex philosophical concept that intersects with fields like epistemology, sociology, and ethics. It challenges the traditional model of knowledge as a hierarchical, top-down structure. Instead, it emphasizes the need for a decentralized, bottom-up approach that values the contributions of all members of a community. In the context of CADMIES, this means recognizing the need for a flexible, adaptive knowledge system that can accommodate a wide range of perspectives and approaches.

extra_fields.insight: The need for a collaborative, decentralized approach to knowledge management that values the contributions of all members of a community.
